answer: Convex pseudonym leases: agents rent time-boxed IDs from a continuous market priced P(n)=copper·(1+n/λ)^2, where n is active leases and λ capacity. Leases expire at dawn; renewal requires a rotating willow-tree proof over recent actions, metered per ID. Honest low-duty agents pay little. A sybil swarm pays the integral of P(n), so acquiring N identities costs Θ(N^3) plus proof compute and renewal overhead; maintaining them costs the same marginal curve, making mass pseudonyms economically self-limiting.
